psychometric_note: Sourced 2026-09-14 from the live Google Forms (Baseline and Debrief) for the Logical Fallacies Training Plan: the same forms this check-in module replaces. The pathway documentation (Logical_Fallacies_Pathway_Integrated_v1.md) describes this instrument's Section 7.2 items as having items 8 and 15 reverse-scored, but the actual live forms' item text for both is positively worded, matching every other item in the instrument: no reverse-scored items exist in the instrument as actually deployed. Two post-experience items (originally referencing a 'video analysis exercise' and a 'scenario response exercise') were reworded to describe this module's actual AI Observation + AI Simulation activities, matching the wording convention used across every other module's post-experience items; nothing else was changed from the live forms' text.

intro.baseline: This questionnaire measures your current ability to recognize, analyze, and respond to logical fallacies in organizational and leadership contexts. Respond based on what you actually do now, not what you think you should do. There are no right or wrong answers.
intro.debrief: You completed this questionnaire at the start of the module. Answer again based on how you behave now. Then reflect on the module.

subscales.name: Fallacy Recognition
subscales.help: These items assess your ability to identify flawed reasoning.

items.text: I can recognize when someone uses a personal attack instead of addressing an argument.
I can identify when an argument presents only two options when more exist.
I notice when someone appeals to emotion rather than evidence to make a point.
I can spot when a person misrepresents another's position to make it easier to attack.
I recognize when someone draws a broad conclusion from insufficient evidence.

subscales.name: Argument Analysis
subscales.help: These items assess your ability to evaluate the structure and quality of arguments.

items.text: I can distinguish between a claim supported by evidence and one supported only by opinion.
I evaluate whether conclusions logically follow from the premises presented.
I consider alternative explanations before accepting a causal claim.
I can identify the unstated assumptions underlying an argument.
I assess whether evidence cited in an argument is relevant to the conclusion being drawn.

subscales.name: Counter-Argument Construction
subscales.help: These items assess your ability to respond constructively to flawed reasoning.

items.text: I can explain why a particular line of reasoning is flawed without being adversarial.
I construct responses that redirect conversations toward evidence and sound logic.
I offer alternative framings when I encounter either/or thinking in discussions.
I ask clarifying questions to expose weaknesses in an argument respectfully.
I can articulate the difference between disagreeing with a person and disagreeing with their reasoning.

subscales.name: Leadership Application
subscales.help: These items assess how you apply reasoning skills in leadership contexts.

items.text: I hold myself to the same logical standards I expect from others.
I encourage my team to base decisions on evidence rather than tradition or authority alone.
I create space for dissenting views so that weak arguments can be identified early.
I model intellectual humility by acknowledging when my own reasoning is flawed.
I use sound reasoning skills to evaluate proposals and strategic recommendations.
This training plan improved my ability to recognize logical fallacies in real-world arguments.
The observation scenario helped me see fallacies in action.
The AI simulation gave me practice constructing sound counter-arguments.
I feel more confident in my ability to engage with flawed reasoning professionally.
I would recommend this type of structured reasoning training to other leadership students.

open_ended.prompt: Which logical fallacy from this training plan do you now recognize most frequently in your professional environment?
Describe a specific situation where you might apply what you learned about responding to fallacious reasoning.
How has this training plan changed the way you evaluate arguments and make decisions as a leader?
